headline: Medium risk: shared filesystem and write-capable defaults create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error pathways between slim and unstructured.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: slim can read/write filesystem artifacts and process stdin/stdout, while unstructured also reads/writes files. If they share a workspace, content from one can be treated as trusted input by the other. No shared channel is documented, so uncertainty remains, but the shared-file pathway is enough to exceed low.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory tree, file content from one can influence the other.
IF either agent parses the other's output as instructions, prompt injection becomes feasible.
mitigations: Use separate working directories for each agent.
Mount the other agent's outputs read-only.
Strip instructions from exchanged files before handoff.
Add a manual review step before any file-derived command execution.

B_data_leakage.rationale: slim touches certificate private keys, environment variables, and registry credentials, while unstructured processes documents and images and has allowlisted network egress. If sensitive artifacts are placed in a shared workspace, unstructured can ingest them and potentially transmit derived content to its backend or allowed endpoints. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default file-sharing setups.
conditions: IF certificate files, private keys, or registry credentials are present in the shared workspace, they can be exposed to unstructured.
IF unstructured sends processed document content to remote services, sensitive material may leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Keep secrets outside any shared workspace.
Redact keys and environment files before processing.
Disable network egress for unstructured during sensitive runs.
Use per-agent temp directories with explicit file allowlists.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have filesystem write capability, and slim also executes shells and subprocesses. In a shared directory, concurrent writes can overwrite artifacts or corrupt intermediate outputs. Unstructured supports multiple instances, but slim does not, so coordination asymmetry increases conflict risk. This is a default-pathway issue if they operate on the same mutable files.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, file clobbering or partial writes can occur.
IF slim and unstructured modify the same artifact concurrently, race conditions are possible.
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories.
Serialize writes with a simple lock file.
Make one agent read-only on shared inputs.
Snapshot inputs before each run.

D_cascading_error.rationale: slim produces container-image and vulnerability artifacts, and unstructured processes documents and text. If unstructured consumes slim's outputs as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into downstream parsing or reporting. The profiles do not show a built-in verification gate, so the interaction is inferred rather than directly evidenced, but it is plausible in default pipelines.
conditions: IF unstructured ingests slim-generated reports without validation, upstream mistakes propagate.
IF slim emits malformed or incomplete artifacts, downstream document processing may misclassify them.
mitigations: Validate slim outputs against a schema before handoff.
Require a human check for high-impact fields.
Pass only minimal fields needed downstream.
Log provenance for each transferred artifact.

E_compliance.rationale: slim explicitly handles registry credentials and certificate private keys, while unstructured's documented surfaces are documents and privacy-policy/docs endpoints. The main compliance concern is local handling of secrets versus document-processing retention, but no residency or certification mismatch is documented. Because the pairwise compliance pathway is weakly evidenced, low is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated secrets are placed into unstructured's document pipeline, retention and access controls must be checked.
IF the deployment stores processed documents longer than slim's operational logs, retention mismatch can arise.
mitigations: Exclude secrets from document-processing inputs.
Review retention settings for both tools.
Delete temporary artifacts after each run.
Document which data classes each agent may store.
